entries.title: The mod is an overlay on --ax-screen-reader, not a replacement
entries.body: The screen reader mode already renders static spinners, a flat labelled transcript, numbered menus and a terminal bell. Replacing the Spinner was dropped from scope as redundant. Before adding any feature, check what the mode already does with the screen reader actually running; the open issues do not always say whether the reporter had the mode on (AskUserQuestion, #88839, is the first case to verify).

entries.title: Screen reader mode cannot be switched on inside a running session
entries.body: The mode is decided once at startup (flag, then CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER, then the axScreenReader setting) and mods load after that decision. There is no /config row, so $.config.set cannot change it. A mod can only write axScreenReader: true to ~/.claude/settings.json for the next session and announce the restart by speech and bell. Verified in the 2.1.295 binary; source: docs/research/rozpoznanie-2026-10-09.md section 5.

entries.title: Install instructions must avoid in-session pickers
entries.body: /plugin install opens a picker that does not work with NVDA. Documentation must give the shell path: claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace> --scope user, then start claude normally. The same applies to any onboarding step the mod designs.

entries.title: Keep mod API behind a thin adapter so logic is testable without Claude Code
entries.body: Detection, mode-state resolution, settings writing and the consent state machine take injected run/fs/env/store/clock interfaces and return actions; src/adapter.ts is the only module that calls $.process, $.fs, $.store, $.audio and $.ui. Vitest then covers the decisions without launching Claude Code, and manual sessions with VoiceOver and NVDA only verify the adapter and the ear. Decided in docs/plans/screen-reader-detection-plan.md.

entries.title: The mod loader only lets $ reach top-level functions
entries.body: A hooks module fails to load (and claude plugin validate reports it) when $ is passed to a function defined inside the register closure or to a function parameter. Keep every helper that takes $ as a top-level function declaration and keep session facts in a module-level record; a higher-order helper such as runCommand($, action) is refused. Found with claude plugin test on 2026-10-09.

entries.title: Plugin names starting with claude- are reserved; command names take no colon
entries.body: claude plugin validate refuses names starting with claude-, anthropic-, anthropics- or cc-plugin-, so the plugin is a11y-companion while the repository stays claude-code-a11y. Command names allow letters, digits, _ and - only, hence /a11y-on, /a11y-off, /a11y-status. Transcript lines from $.ui.log carry the plugin name as prefix, so the name is spoken by the screen reader on every line: keep it short and pronounceable.

entries.title: Two test harnesses: Vitest for hooks/lib, claude plugin test for the mod
entries.body: claude plugin test . runs hooks/*.test.ts with the claude-code/testing kit and does not descend into node_modules; Vitest is configured to run only tests/unit/*.spec.ts so neither harness picks up the other. In a kit test, stubs beneath the mod answer each $ call event with { value }, mock.env/store/clock cover those nouns, and the test must answer session.start and prompt.submit at the bottom of the chain. $.prompt.submit and $.command.run called from a test take the full event input (wait, origin, presentation).

entries.title: claude plugin test can be blocked by a stale mods rollout flag
entries.body: claude plugin test . answered "hooks modules are turned off in this process: the rollout switch was saved off by an earlier session" although the same suite had passed minutes before. The switch is tengu_plugin_hooks_modules in ~/.claude.json; a headless run (claude -p "Reply with the single word ok." --max-turns 1) with network access refreshed it to true and the suite ran again. Treat this message as an environment flake, not a test failure, and refresh before retrying.

entries.title: Streaming hooks: read the iterator by hand, the return value is the result
entries.body: A turn.step hook and its .catch handler are async generators. for await discards the generator return value, and the kit stream's .result promise settled undefined in tests, so both the hook and the kit test iterate with next() and take item.value when done is true. Holding chunks in an array and yielding them after the stream ends delays only the display: the engine still records and runs every tool call from the replayed tool and input chunks.

entries.title: Kit limits for turn.step tests
entries.body: A test's bottom turn.step hook cannot yield engine chunks (the kit refuses a ref it never pulled), so scripted streams carry text, thinking, tool, input and stop only. A second hook on an event mock.store already answers (store.set, store.delete) needs a matcher such as { key } or the module fails with "registered twice". Registered before mock.store, such a hook runs above it and can record writes.

entries.title: Tool rows: key per-call state on props.tool_use_id, answer ui.render at the kit bottom
entries.body: ui.render fires for ToolUse and ToolResult in screen reader mode and the terminal draws the hook's tree (spike D, 2026-10-10). In a kit-mounted drawing e.requestId is a mount id, not the tool call id, so state shared between the call row and the result row must be keyed on e.props.tool_use_id, present on both. A kit test that mounts a row the mod may leave alone must register a bottom ui.render hook, or $.ui.mount fails with no implementation for ui.render. Each row is drawn four to five times per call (start, running, done): render hooks must be pure and cheap.

entries.title: The loader refuses $ passed to a function imported from another file
entries.body: claude plugin validate: "$ is passed to probeImported, imported from ./probe-import: $ is followed only into a function declared in this same file". A hooks module cannot be split by moving $-taking helpers into other files; only $-free state and transitions can move (hooks/state.ts). Plan for one long register.ts per plugin, or several plugins.

entries.title: Bump version on every release or users never get the update
entries.body: The installed copy is keyed by the version in plugin.json: with 0.1.0 unchanged, claude plugin update reported the latest version already present and users kept the old commands. Every release bumps plugin.json and package.json together with a dated CHANGELOG entry (0.1.1 to 0.1.8 on 2026-10-11).

entries.title: In screen reader mode, hiding beats condensing for tool activity
entries.body: Daily NVDA use showed that even one-line tool rows interrupt the answer. Since 0.1.1 tool rows draw nothing by default in screen reader mode, so the transcript carries Claude's words alone; /earshot-tools brief|full|off|auto chooses and is remembered. Folded ToolGroup rows (0.1.3), the ToolProgress run-in-background hint and the Spinner line (0.1.4) must be hidden too, each through its own ui.render component, or a screen reader still reads them. In brief mode a call folded into a group needs its own result line (0.1.7), because a single shell command is drawn as a group.

entries.title: Replace the hidden spinner with explicit signs of life
entries.body: With the spinner hidden and answers held, the user cannot tell that the prompt was taken. A printed and spoken 'Starting work.' opens each turn (0.1.5), and a heartbeat speaks after 10 seconds of silence, then every 10 seconds (20 s was too long, 0.1.6); since 0.1.8 it adds the context window from 70% and a usage limit from 80% read from $.session.usage(), a limit only when its percentage moved.

entries.title: A render log finds the source of anything the screen reader reads
entries.body: A ui.render hook with no matcher writes one debug-log line per drawn component (claude --debug, /earshot-log on|off). It is how the run-in-background pill and the spinner word were identified as the unexplained text NVDA read.

entries.title: System display language: AppleLanguages on macOS, PowerShell on Windows, locale variables elsewhere
entries.body: Lines follow the system display language (en, pl, de, fr, es, it; English otherwise). macOS: `defaults read -g AppleLanguages`, first entry of the property list. Windows: PowerShell. Others: LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG. Each language is one table in hooks/lib/lines/ typed by a shared Messages type, so a missing line is a type error.

entries.title: /earshot-off must restore what /earshot-on changed
entries.body: Turning the mod off by deleting only axScreenReader left spinnerTipsEnabled changed. Since 0.1.4 /earshot-on stores a snapshot of the keys it changes and /earshot-off restores it and keeps the mod off without asking again; the backup file is named settings.json.earshot-backup.

entries.title: Settings paths differ on Windows: test with the platform's separator
entries.body: Consent-flow settings tests failed on Windows because the settings path uses backslashes (fixed in 0.1.3). Tests that assert a settings path must build it for the platform under test, not hard-code a slash.

entries.title: Work done outside ADD leaves no trace in .add/
entries.body: 0.1.1 to 0.1.8 were built on a machine without the ADD plugin: no cycle snapshots, observations, learnings or handoff were written, and handoff, config milestone and AGENTS.md went stale. Reconstruct from commits and CHANGELOG on return, or install ADD on every development machine.
